name: Firebase
tagline: Google's app platform: Firestore, Realtime Database and Data Connect, plus auth, functions and hosting.
description: Firebase is Google's backend platform for mobile and web apps. Its databases are Cloud Firestore (a serverless document store with realtime listeners, offline persistence in the SDKs, vector search and TTL), the original Realtime Database (a JSON tree synced over websockets), and Data Connect, which puts a GraphQL layer over Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL. Around them sit Authentication, Cloud Functions, Hosting, Storage, Remote Config and analytics. Firebase is the fastest way for a small team to ship a synced mobile app, but security rules, query limits and per-operation billing need care as usage grows.

pricing.notes: Spark plan is free with quotas; Blaze is pay-as-you-go, billed per document read/write, storage and egress.

scale.notes: Firestore scales automatically and offers multi-region locations; Realtime Database shards per instance.

strengths: Realtime listeners and offline persistence built into the mobile and web SDKs
One console for database, auth, functions, hosting and analytics
Serverless Firestore scales without capacity planning
Security Rules let clients talk to the database directly
Data Connect adds relational Postgres when documents are not enough
weaknesses: Per-read billing can surprise you at scale or with chatty listeners
Firestore queries are restricted: no joins, limited OR/inequality combinations
Security Rules are easy to get wrong and hard to test
Locked to Google Cloud with no self-hosted option
useCases: Mobile apps needing realtime sync and offline support
MVPs and startups that want auth and database in one
Push notifications and remote config alongside app data
